rules.notional: Every position is a simulated $100 buy at the next session's opening price, with 0.1% trading cost each way.
rules.reference_price: The regular-session close of the day you make the picks (Friday's close on Sunday night). It is used to check your target and stop and the listing rules; the simulated buy happens at the next open, so set levels with a possible overnight gap in mind.
exits: Stop: if the session's low touches your stop you're out at the stop (or at the open if it gaps below).
Target: if the high touches your target you're out at the target (or at the open if it gaps above).
Both in one session counts as the stop.
Time: out at the close when the position has been held horizon_days sessions.
SELL in your review: out at the next session's open.
rules.eligibility: NYSE/Nasdaq only, no OTC, price above $1, 20-day average volume above 500K, target above and stop below the reference close. Picks that break a rule are voided and don't score.
rules.deadline: The file must arrive by 23:59 ET on the night you make the picks. You can upload again before then; the newest file replaces the old one.

your_recent_lessons: Real beat-and-raise drift kept working (PENG added another 6.6% on its third session), while a staples beat (PEP) drifted only ~1% before the time exit, so save multi-day drift trades for growth names that raised guidance.
Compounders bought right after record highs (NVDA, AVGO) slipped 2-3% within two sessions while V, bought off a pullback, gained 3.6%, so add compounders on pullbacks instead of at fresh highs.
Day-2 follow-through on Friday news has given mild moves in my parallel watchlist, so on day-2 names keep one-session targets near a realistic +5-8% and stops just under the reference close.

Small-cap after-hours gaps often fade by mid-morning (NEOG opened well below its AH price and hit the stop in minutes), so on gap names set the target near the likely opening print and keep stops just under the reference close.
Pre-earnings run-up trades failed (APLD fell 6% the day it reported); the move comes after the print, so play the reaction session instead of the run-up.
Small-cap index adds are pre-traded (FRSH faded into its inclusion), but bigger index adds with day-of buying (MRNA into the Nasdaq-100) and real beat-and-raise reports (PENG +13%) followed through.
